precepts.text: Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal. That is why she said our fathers worshipped in this mountain: when we first came into the land, the first place we came into would have been called Samaria, and the first altars were set up in Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. When the nation split, the northern kingdom went back up top and worshipped there; but God called his home Jerusalem, where he set up his temple. Notice also: as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half against mount Gerizim and half against mount Ebal; and the strangers were conversant in the laws of God. When we came into the land we had a mixed multitude among us, and they had to learn the laws; we taught them how to keep the Sabbath day: neither thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor the stranger that is within thy gates.
precepts.point: Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews. When he says Jews, he is talking about all Israel. We know what God's will is for us, for his people, and for the nations, and our job is to teach those things, and in teaching them, to gather in one the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The woman at the well said, “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. On the map, the mountains above the well are Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. Joshua 8 shows why she said it: “Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron: and they offered thereon burnt offerings unto the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings.” “And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.”

When we first came into the land, the first place we came into was what would be called Samaria, and the first altars were set up in Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. That is why, when the nation split, the northern kingdom went back up top and worshipped there: this is the place where we worshipped initially. But God called his home Jerusalem; that is where he set up his temple.

Read on: “And all Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”. The blessings went up on the children of Israel, and the cursing was on Mount Ebal.

“There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.” When we came into the land we had a mixed multitude of the other nations among us, and they were conversant in the laws of God. They had to learn the laws. We taught them how to keep the Sabbath day: six days you do your work, and on the seventh no work, neither your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor the stranger that is within thy gates.

Then Christ answered her: “Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” There was a time coming, 70 AD, when Jerusalem would be toppled by the Romans, and neither the mountains of Samaria nor Jerusalem would matter, because he was destroying it. His purpose was to gather in one the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.text: How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.
precepts.point: Joshua drew not his hand back until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai, meaning the children were put to death also. This was not new: at Sihon's cities Israel utterly destroyed the men, the women, and the little ones. The children's song teaching that Christ loves all the children of every nation alike does not stand with these scriptures; the Lord's love is toward the children of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” At Ai, “all that fell that day, both of men and women, were twelve thousand”. Women are casualties of war.

That stands as a warning for the sisters serving unrepented in the militaries of the nations, standing stiffly for the oppressor, a backsliding daughter compassing a man. When Christ comes back he is coming to kill, and a uniform and a weapon will not save; men and women will be dying alike, as they did at Ai. It is best in these last days for a woman to stand by and support her own man and her own nation, not another nation.

precepts.text: We took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city; we left none to remain.
precepts.point: Joshua drew not his hand back until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai, meaning the children were put to death also. This was not new: at Sihon's cities Israel utterly destroyed the men, the women, and the little ones. The children's song teaching that Christ loves all the children of every nation alike does not stand with these scriptures; the Lord's love is toward the children of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
“For Joshua drew not his hand back, wherewith he stretched out the spear, until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai.” All the inhabitants means the children were put to death also. This was not new. At Sihon’s cities: “And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city, we left none to remain”.

So the children’s song teaching that Christ loves all the children of every nation alike does not stand with these scriptures. The Lord’s love is toward the children of Israel.

precepts.text: Today's peace offering is keeping the commandments.
precepts.point: The Most High hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land; if you do not want the Lord to have a controversy with you, keep the laws. And keeping the laws is more than beards, fringes, borders of blue, and not eating pork: it is purging the unfruitful spirits you know dwell inside you, the jealousy, envy, covetousness, malice, hatred, grudging, backbiting, murmuring, and gossip.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
Joshua “offered thereon burnt offerings unto the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings.” We are still under the law of sacrifice today, but the sacrifice is your body, not the blood of bulls and goats: you sacrifice time, money, pain and labor to push this truth and do the work, spiritual sacrifices through your works by keeping the laws.

“He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.” The peace offering today is keeping the commandments. Under grace, peace is a dispensation: the more sin you commit, the less peace you will have. So keep the commandments, and do not frustrate the grace and peace the Most High has with you.

precepts.text: The Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land; keep the laws so the controversy is not with you.
precepts.point: The Most High hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land; if you do not want the Lord to have a controversy with you, keep the laws. And keeping the laws is more than beards, fringes, borders of blue, and not eating pork: it is purging the unfruitful spirits you know dwell inside you, the jealousy, envy, covetousness, malice, hatred, grudging, backbiting, murmuring, and gossip.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
Joshua wrote upon the stones “a copy of the law of Moses” in the presence of all the children of Israel. “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” If you do not want the Lord to have a controversy with you, keep the laws.

And keeping the laws is more than beards, fringes, borders of blue, and not eating pork. It is purging the unfruitful spirits you know dwell inside you: the jealousy, envy, covetousness, malice, hatred, grudging, backbiting, murmuring and gossip.

precepts.text: There shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord; the order of officers and judges is rehearsed in the body today.
precepts.point: Rehearse means practice, and practice makes perfect: there are rehearsals every day, classes and meetings for the men, the women, and the children, because this is not our rest.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
“there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord”. Why does the body set up rank instead of saying I only follow Christ? Because we are commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord. All Israel stood before the ark in order, “their elders, and officers, and their judges”, half over against mount Gerizim and half over against mount Ebal, as Moses commanded. Reading the wars and works of Joshua, Moses, and the officers, judges and elders, we practice what our forefathers did, in order, as an organized army.

Rehearse means practice, and practice makes perfect. So there are rehearsals every day, classes and meetings for the men, the women and the children, because this is not our rest.

precepts.text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.
precepts.point: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua read not before all the congregation, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them: those were the strangers that fell in line with Israel, with the fear of the Lord in them, as Rahab had.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
Joshua read “the blessings and cursings, according to all that is written in the book of the law.” Moses set them before the people this way: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live”.

Heaven and earth are called to record: everything we do is recorded. Life and death, blessing and cursing, are set before us. We tell our neighbor God bless you, but by the same book the Most High and Christ will curse you too if you do not keep the laws. It is the one thing left optional, so choose life, for it is not just you that pays but thy seed as well.

precepts.text: Keep my commandments, and live; life is keeping the commandments.
precepts.point: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua read not before all the congregation, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them: those were the strangers that fell in line with Israel, with the fear of the Lord in them, as Rahab had.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why: “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” The life set before Israel in the blessings and cursings is the keeping of the commandments of the Most High; that is what life is. Death is the wages of sin. Joshua read every word of the law before all the congregation because that law is life to the one who keeps it, so choose life.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death; sin is what brings the cursing and the death.
precepts.point: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua read not before all the congregation, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them: those were the strangers that fell in line with Israel, with the fear of the Lord in them, as Rahab had.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why: “For the wages of sin is death”. The cursings Joshua read are what sin brings; sin is what brings the cursing and the death. Life is the keeping of the commandments, death is the wages of sin, and the Most High left that one thing optional: blessing or cursing, life or death. Choose life, for it is not just you that pays but thy seed as well.

precepts.text: Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life; the blessing at the last page of the book.
precepts.point: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua read not before all the congregation, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them: those were the strangers that fell in line with Israel, with the fear of the Lord in them, as Rahab had.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
How do you become blessed? Read the last page of the book: “Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.” A few verses before your Bible says the end, it says keep the commandments. So no man in his right mind can say the laws are done away with; that is justifying wickedness.

The blessings Joshua read before all the congregation are the blessings at the last page of the book, and they come the same way. Keep the sabbath holy, leave the swine alone, dress in modesty, and keep the commandments if you want the blessings.

points: God told Joshua he had already given him Ai, yet commanded an ambush behind the city. The victory is ordained, but it must be won God's way.
Israel fled as commanded, the men of Ai left their city open, and the smoke of the city rose behind them. Victory came through obedience.

note.label: War of the Gods

points: With the accursed thing purged, the Lord said unto Joshua, Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the people of war with thee and go up to Ai; see, I have given into thy hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: This time the spoil thereof and the cattle shall ye take for a prey unto yourselves, unlike Jericho where everything was consecrated to the treasury of the Lord; and the command was to lay an ambush for the city behind it.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour and sent them away by night to lie in ambush behind the city, not very far from it, always ready. These were warriors, men of courage, but none of that matters unless the spirit is right with the Lord first.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings
